result:
`scripts/backup.sh --dry-run SOURCE DEST` now prints every destination path it would create plus a "would back up" line, and creates nothing — not even the dated folder. I ran both modes against a temp directory: the dry run left DEST absent, and a normal run copied as before.

```sh
dry=
if [ "${1:-}" = --dry-run ]; then
    dry=1
    shift
fi
src=${1:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
dest=${2:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
target=$dest/$(date +%F)
if [ -n "$dry" ]; then
    (cd "$src" && find . ! -name . | sed "s|^\./|$target/|")
    echo "would back up $src to $target"
    exit 0
fi
```

The README's Backup section now shows the `[--dry-run]` usage and describes the option in place of "Options: none."

The flag must come first; `backup.sh SOURCE DEST --dry-run` ignores it and does a real copy. The dry run also does not say which files already exist in the target and would be overwritten. I left the version files alone; say if you want this released as a version bump.
